comments.text: A 'multi-point' checklist from ANYONE selling you a car is worthless.  I once bought a truck from a Ford dealership that had the "Ford Pre-owned certification".  I found out a day later the truck had been in a collision and had several thousands of dollars of repairs done to it.  Because my insurance company told me, when I called them to give them the VIN and get my insurance in order, that it had been smashed.  The vehicle looked good, so the repairs were obviously well done.  The problem is, loss of value.  Because eventually if I went to sell it, that accident info would likely come up, therefore making the truck worth thousands less than it would normally be.  Fortunately the dealer took it back and tore up the sales contract the next day when I went in and raised hell.   DO NOT TRUST any report from anyone selling you a car.  A CarFax report is a good idea. HOWEVER that accident on that truck I bought did NOT show up in the CarFax !  So CarFax is not always accurate either!

comments.author: @pikestance8851
comments.text:
I prefer to buy from a dealership, especially a used vehicle. I know people who work for dealerships, and I know they inspect and repair any issues with the car. They did it when we sold my father's Mercedes. It had a bunch of issues, and they repaired every single one. We also got a good deal, but it might have been because a family member actually worked there. 
Audi is absolutely a good buy. When I purchased my Audi. I researched and compared it to Mercedes. Audi is more reliable than Mercedes (and cheaper) and, dollar for dollar, more affordable than a BMW. Moreover, I bought an A5 Sportsback, and it had excellent resale value. If you want a high-end German car, you can't go wrong with an Audi. I have never met a single person unhappy with an Audi. Now, old-time buyers do complain about the newer cars, but hey, that's not surprising. I also bought a certified pre-owned car from Mercedes for my wife (she loves Mercedes). We were debating whether or not to buy a Mazda. The Mercedes SUV was a little cheaper than the Mazda (but it was slightly larger). My wife didn't care; it was  Mercedes. Again, I could not be any happier with the choice. My wife has an expression: "You get what you pay for.... what do you expect?" There's a reason why some things are cheap.

comments.text: Before you buy a car, go talk to a mechanic about what you are thinking about buying. They will tell you what not to buy and what you should get if you want something reliable. Talk to several. Take notes. If you want a luxury car and you can't afford to buy one, you really can't afford a used one. Lease it. If you can't afford to lease, you can't afford it at all.  My next car will be an off lease Lexus or Toyota.
